 31214                                  IsEOF:
 31215                                  	;cmp	word [es:bp+0Dh],0FF6h
 31216 00005391 26817E0DF60F            	CMP	word [ES:BP+DPB.MAX_CLUSTER],4096-10 ; is this 16 bit fat?
 31217 00005397 730B                    	JAE	short EOF16			; yes, check for eof there
 31218                                  
 31219                                  ;J.K. 8/27/86
 31220                                  ;Modified to accept 0FF0h as an eof. This is to handle the diskfull case
 31221                                  ;of any media that has "F0"(Other) as a MediaByte.
 31222                                  ;Hopely, this does not create any side effect for those who may use any value
 31223                                  ;other than "FF8-FFF" as an EOF for their own file.
 31224                                  
 31225 00005399 81FBF00F                	cmp	bx,0FF0h
 31226 0000539D 7404                    	je	short IsEOF_other
 31227                                  
 31228 0000539F 81FBF80F                	CMP	BX,0FF8h		; do the 12 bit compare
 31229                                  IsEOF_other:
 31230 000053A3 C3                      	retn
 31231                                  EOF16:
 31232 000053A4 83FBF8                  	CMP	BX,0FFF8h		; 16 bit compare
 31233 000053A7 C3                      	retn
 31234                                  
 31235                                  ; DOSCODE:9511h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 31236                                  
 31237                                  ;Break	<UNPACK -- UNPACK FAT ENTRIES>
 31238                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31239                                  ;
 31240                                  ; Procedur Name : UNPACK
 31241                                  ;
 31242                                  ; Inputs:
 31243                                  ;	BX = Cluster number (may be full 16-bit quantity)
 31244                                  ;	ES:BP = Base of drive parameters
 31245                                  ; Outputs:
 31246                                  ;	DI = Contents of FAT for given cluster (may be full 16-bit quantity)
 31247                                  ;	Zero set means DI=0 (free cluster)
 31248                                  ;	Carry set means error (currently user FAILed to I 24)
 31249                                  ; SI Destroyed, No other registers affected. Fatal error if cluster too big.
 31250                                  ;
 31251                                  ; NOTE: if BX = 0 then DI = contents of CL0FATENTRY
 31252                                  ;
 31253                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31254                                  	
 31255                                  	; 25/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 31256                                  	; DOSCODE:94B5h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
 31257                                  
 31258                                  	; 20/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 31259                                  UNPACK:
 31260                                  	; MSDOS 6.0			; M014 - Start
 31261 000053A8 09DB                    	or	bx,bx			; Q: are we unpacking cluster 0
 31262 000053AA 7507                    	jnz	short up_cont		; N: proceed with normal unpack
 31263 000053AC 8B3E[8100]              	mov	di,[CL0FATENTRY]	; Y: return value in CL0FATENTRY
 31264 000053B0 09FF                    	or	di,di 			; return z if di=0
 31265 000053B2 C3                      	retn				; done
 31266                                  up_cont:				; M014 - End
 31267                                  	; MSDOS 3.3 & MSDOS 6.0
 31268                                  	;cmp	bx,[es:bp+0Dh]
 31269 000053B3 263B5E0D                	CMP	BX,[ES:BP+DPB.MAX_CLUSTER]
 31270 000053B7 7726                    	JA	short HURTFAT
 31271 000053B9 E8D500                  	CALL	MAPCLUSTER
 31272 000053BC 721E                    	jc	short _DoContext
 31273 000053BE 8B3D                    	MOV	DI,[DI]
 31274 000053C0 750E                    	JNZ	short High12		; MZ if high 12 bits, go get 'em
 31275 000053C2 268B760D                	MOV	SI,[ES:BP+DPB.MAX_CLUSTER] ; MZ is this 16-bit fat?
 31276 000053C6 81FEF60F                	CMP	SI,4096-10
 31277 000053CA 720C                    	JB	short Unpack12		; MZ No, go 'AND' off bits
 31278 000053CC 09FF                    	OR	DI,DI			; MZ set zero condition code, clears carry
 31279 000053CE EB0C                    	JMP	SHORT _DoContext 	; MZ go do context
 31280                                  High12:
 31281 000053D0 D1EF                    	SHR	DI,1
 31282 000053D2 D1EF                    	SHR	DI,1
 31283 000053D4 D1EF                    	SHR	DI,1
 31284 000053D6 D1EF                    	SHR	DI,1
 31285                                  Unpack12:

 31287                                  _DoContext:
 31288 000053DC 16                      	PUSH	SS
 31289 000053DD 1F                      	POP	DS
 31290 000053DE C3                      	retn

 31296 000053E6 B488                    	MOV	AH,Allowed_FAIL+80h ; 88h

 31302                                  ;

 31304 000053F1 E8CCFD                  	call	FATAL

 31308 000053F9 F9                      	STC				; User said FAIL

 31311                                  hurtfat_retn:
 31312 000053FB C3                      	retn

 31316                                  ;Break	<PACK -- PACK FAT ENTRIES>
 31317                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31318                                  ;
 31319                                  ; Procedure Name : PACK
 31320                                  ;
 31321                                  ; Inputs:
 31322                                  ;	BX = Cluster number
 31323                                  ;	DX = Data
 31324                                  ;	ES:BP = Pointer to drive DPB
 31325                                  ; Outputs:
 31326                                  ;	The data is stored in the FAT at the given cluster.
 31327                                  ;	SI,DX,DI all destroyed
 31328                                  ;	Carry set means error (currently user FAILed to I 24)
 31329                                  ;	No other registers affected
 31330                                  ;
 31331                                  ; NOTE: if BX = 0 then data in DX is stored in CL0FATENTRY.
 31332                                  ;
 31333                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31334                                  
 31335                                  	; 02/01/2024
 31336                                  	; 25/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 31337                                  	; 20/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 31338                                  PACK:
 31339                                  	; MSDOS 6.0			; M014 - start
 31340 000053FC 09DB                    	or	bx,bx			; Q: are we packing cluster 0

 31342 00005400 8916[8100]              	mov	[CL0FATENTRY],dx	; Y: place value in CL0FATENTRY
 31343 00005404 C3                      	retn				; done
 31344                                  p_cont:					; M014 - end
 31345                                  	; MSDOS 3.3 & MSDOS 6.0

 31351 0000540F B104                    	MOV	CL,4
 31352 00005411 D3E2                    	SHL	DX,CL
 31353 00005413 59                      	POP	CX
 31354 00005414 83E60F                  	AND	SI,0FH			; leave in original low 4 bits
 31355 00005417 EB13                    	JMP	SHORT PACKIN

 31359 0000541F 7309                    	JAE	short Pack16		; MZ yes, go clobber original data
 31360 00005421 81E600F0                	AND	SI,0F000h		; MZ leave in upper 4 bits of original

 31452                                  ;Break	<MAPCLUSTER - BUFFER A FAT SECTOR>
 31453                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31454                                  ;
 31455                                  ; Procedure Name : MAPCLUSTER
 31456                                  ;
 31457                                  ; Inputs:
 31458                                  ;	ES:BP Points to DPB
 31459                                  ;	BX Is cluster number
 31460                                  ; Function:
 31461                                  ;	Get a pointer to the cluster
 31462                                  ; Outputs:
 31463                                  ;	DS:DI Points to contents of FAT for given cluster
 31464                                  ;	DS:SI Points to start of buffer
 31465                                  ;	Zero Not set if cluster data is in high 12 bits of word
 31466                                  ;	Zero set if cluster data is in low 12 or 16 bits
 31467                                  ;	Carry set if failed.
 31468                                  ; SI is destroyed.
 31469                                  ;
 31470                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31471                                  
 31472                                  	; 20/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 31473                                  	; DOSCODE:9601h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 31474                                  	; 27/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 31475                                  	; DOSCODE:95A5h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
 31476                                  
 31477                                  MAPCLUSTER:
 31478                                  	; IBMDOS.COM (MSDOS 3.3, 1987) - Offset 5A15h
 31479 00005491 C606[7805]00            	MOV	BYTE [CLUSSPLIT],0
 31480                                  	;SAVE	<AX,BX,CX,DX>
 31481 00005496 50                      	push	ax
 31482 00005497 53                      	push	bx
 31483 00005498 51                      	push	cx
 31484 00005499 52                      	push	dx
 31485 0000549A 89D8                    	MOV	AX,BX			; AX = BX
 31486 0000549C 26817E0DF60F            	CMP	word [ES:BP+DPB.MAX_CLUSTER],4096-10  ; MZ 16 bit fat?
 31487 000054A2 7302                    	JAE	short Map16		; MZ yes, do 16 bit algorithm
 31488 000054A4 D1E8                    	SHR	AX,1			; AX = BX/2
 31489                                  Map16:	
 31490                                  	; MSDOS 6.0			; MZ skip prev => AX=2*BX
 31491 000054A6 31FF                    	XOR	DI,DI ; *		; >32mb fat ;AN000;
 31492                                  	; MSDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)
 31493 000054A8 01D8                    	ADD	AX,BX			; AX = 1.5*fat = byte offset in fat
 31494 000054AA 11FF                    	ADC	DI,DI ; * MSDOS 6.0	; >32mb fat ;DI is zero before op;AN000;
 31495 000054AC 268B4E02                	MOV	CX,[ES:BP+DPB.SECTOR_SIZE]
 31496                                  
 31497                                  ;IF FastDiv
 31498                                  ;
 31499                                  ; Gross hack: 99% of all disks have 512 bytes per sector. We test for this
 31500                                  ; case and apply a really fast algorithm to get the desired results
 31501                                  ;
 31502                                  ; Divide method takes 157+4*4=173 (MOV and DIV)
 31503                                  ; Fast method takes 39+20*4=119
 31504                                  ;
 31505                                  ; This saves a bunch.
 31506                                  
 31507 000054B0 81F90002                	CMP	CX,512			; 4  Is this 512 byte sector?
 31508 000054B4 7510                    	jne	short _DoDiv		; 4  for no jump
 31509 000054B6 89C2                    	MOV	DX,AX			; 2  get set for remainder
 31510 000054B8 81E2FF01                	AND	DX,512-1		; 4  Form remainder
 31511 000054BC 88E0                    	MOV	AL,AH			; 2  Quotient in formation in AL
 31512                                  	; MDOS 3.3
 31513                                  	;shr	al,1	
 31514                                  	; MDOS 6.0
 31515 000054BE D1EF                    	shr	di,1			; 2
 31516 000054C0 D0D8                    	rcr	al,1			; 2
 31517                                  	; MDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)
 31518 000054C2 30E4                    	xor	ah,ah			; 3
 31519 000054C4 EB04                    	jmp	short DivDone		; 16
 31520                                  _DoDiv:
 31521                                  ;ENDIF
 31522                                  	; MSDOS 3.3
 31523                                  	;xor	dx,dx
 31524                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 31525 000054C6 89FA                    	mov	dx,di			; 2
 31526                                  	; MSDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)	
 31527 000054C8 F7F1                    	DIV	CX			; 155 AX is FAT sector # DX is sector index
 31528                                  ;IF FastDiv
 31529                                  DivDone:
 31530                                  ;ENDIF
 31531                                  	;add	ax,[es:bp+6]
 31532 000054CA 26034606                	ADD	AX,[ES:BP+DPB.FIRST_FAT]
 31533 000054CE 49                      	DEC	CX			; CX is sector size - 1
 31534                                  	;SAVE	<AX,DX,CX>
 31535 000054CF 50                      	push	ax
 31536 000054D0 52                      	push	dx
 31537 000054D1 51                      	push	cx
 31538 000054D2 89C2                    	MOV	DX,AX
 31539                                  
 31540                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 31541                                  	; 22/09/2023
 31542                                  	;MOV	word [HIGH_SECTOR],0 ; *! ;F.C. >32mb  low sector #
 31543                                  	;
 31544                                  	; MDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)
 31545                                  	;XOR	AL,AL	   ; *
 31546                                  	;MOV	SI,1	   ; *
 31547                                  	;;invoke GETBUFFRB ; *
 31548                                  	;call	GETBUFFRB  ; *
 31549                                  	; 22/09/2023
 31550 000054D4 E8C802                  	call	GETBUFFRC  ; *!
 31551                                  
 31552                                  	;RESTORE <CX,AX,DX>		; CX is sec siz-1, AX is offset in sec
 31553 000054D7 59                      	pop	cx
 31554 000054D8 58                      	pop	ax
 31555 000054D9 5A                      	pop	dx
 31556 000054DA 724C                    	JC	short MAP_POP
 31557                                  
 31558 000054DC C536[E205]              	LDS	SI,[CURBUF]
 31559                                  	;;lea	di,[si+16]
 31560                                  	;lea	di,[si+20] ; MSDOS 6.0
 31561 000054E0 8D7C14                  	LEA	DI,[SI+BUFINSIZ]
 31562 000054E3 01C7                    	ADD	DI,AX
 31563 000054E5 39C8                    	CMP	AX,CX
 31564 000054E7 752C                    	JNZ	short MAPRET
 31565 000054E9 8A05                    	MOV	AL,[DI]
 31566                                  	;Context DS		 	;hkn; SS is DOSDATA
 31567 000054EB 16                      	push	ss
 31568 000054EC 1F                      	pop	ds	
 31569 000054ED FE06[7805]              	INC	BYTE [CLUSSPLIT]
 31570 000054F1 A2[8E05]                	MOV	[CLUSSAVE],AL
 31571 000054F4 8916[9005]              	MOV	[CLUSSEC],DX
 31572                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 31573 000054F8 C706[9205]0000          	MOV	WORD [CLUSSEC+2],0      ;F.C. >32mb	;AN000;
 31574 000054FE 42                      	INC	DX
 31575                                  
 31576                                  	; 22/09/2023
 31577                                  	;MOV	word [HIGH_SECTOR],0 ; *! ;F.C. >32mb FAT sector <32mb ;AN000;
 31578                                  	;
 31579                                  	; MDOS 3.3 (& MSDOS 6.0)
 31580                                  	;XOR	AL,AL	   ; *

 31630                                  ; Procedure Name : FATREAD_SFT
 31631                                  ;
 31632                                  ; Inputs:
 31633                                  ;	ES:DI points to an SFT for the drive of intrest (local only,
 31634                                  ;		giving a NET SFT will produce system crashing results).
 31635                                  ;	DS DOSDATA
 31636                                  ; Function:
 31637                                  ;	Can be used by an SFT routine (like CLOSE) to invalidate buffers
 31638                                  ;	if disk changed.
 31639                                  ;	In other respects, same as FATREAD_CDS.
 31640                                  ;	(note ES:DI destroyed!)
 31641                                  ; Outputs:
 31642                                  ;	Carry set if error (currently user FAILed to I 24)
 31643                                  ; NOTE: This routine may cause FATREAD_CDS to "miss" a disk change
 31644                                  ;	as far as invalidating curdir_ID is concerned.
 31645                                  ;	Since getting a true disk changed on this call is a screw up
 31646                                  ;	anyway, that's the way it goes.
 31647                                  ;
 31648                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------

 31654                                  	; 15/12/2022

 32523                                  ;
 32524                                  ; Procedure Name : PointComp
 32525                                  ; Inputs:
 32526                                  ;         DS:SI & ES:DI
 32527                                  ; Function:
 32528                                  ;          Checks for ((SI==DI) && (ES==DS))
 32529                                  ;	   Assumes that pointers are normalized for the
 32530                                  ;	   same segment
 32531                                  ;
 32532                                  ; Compare DS:SI to ES:DI (or DS:DI to ES:SI) for equality
 32533                                  ; DO NOT USE FOR < or >
 32534                                  ; No Registers altered

 32538                                  POINTCOMP:
 32539                                  	; 31/07/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 32540                                  	; IBMDOS.COM (MSDOS 3.3, 1987) - Offset 5D84h

 32542 00005792 750A                    	jnz	short _ret_label	; return if nz
 32543                                  	;jnz	short placehead_retn

 32545 00005795 52                      	PUSH	DX
 32546 00005796 8CD9                    	MOV	CX,DS

 32557                                  ;Break	<GETBUFFR, GETBUFFRB -- GET A SECTOR INTO A BUFFER>
 32558                                  
 32559                                  ;**	GetBuffr - Get a non-FAT Sector into a Buffer
 32560                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 32561                                  ;	GetBuffr does normal ( non-FAT ) sector buffering
 32562                                  ;	It gets the specified local sector into one of the I/O buffers
 32563                                  ;	and shuffles the queue
 32564                                  ; 
 32565                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = 0 means sector must be pre-read
 32566                                  ;		       ELSE no pre-read
 32567                                  ;		(DX) = Desired physical sector number	      (LOW)
 32568                                  ;		HIGH_SECTOR = Desired physical sector number (HIGH)
 32569                                  ;		(ES:BP) = Pointer to drive parameters
 32570                                  ;		ALLOWED set in case of INT 24
 32571                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error (user FAIL response to INT24)
 32572                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 32573                                  ;		CURBUF Points to the Buffer for the sector
 32574                                  ;		    the buffer type bits OF buf_flags = 0, caller must set it
 32575                                  ;	USES	AX, BX, CX, SI, DI, Flags
 32576                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 32577                                  
 32578                                  ;**	GetBuffrb - Get a FAT Sector into a Buffer
 32579                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 32580                                  ;	GetBuffrb reads a sector from the FAT file system's FAT table.
 32581                                  ;	It gets the specified sector into one of the I/O buffers
 32582                                  ;	and shuffles the queue. We need a special entry point so that
 32583                                  ;	we can read the alternate FAT sector if the first read fails, also
 32584                                  ;	so we can mark the buffer as a FAT sector.
 32585                                  ; 
 32586                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = 0 means sector must be pre-read
 32587                                  ;		       ELSE no pre-read
 32588                                  ;		(DX) = Desired physical sector number	     (LOW)
 32589                                  ;		(SI) != 0
 32590                                  ;		HIGH_SECTOR = Desired physical sector number (HIGH)
 32591                                  ;		(ES:BP) = Pointer to drive parameters
 32592                                  ;		ALLOWED set in case of INT 24
 32593                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error (user FAIL response to INT24)
 32594                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 32595                                  ;		CUR ddBUF Points to the Buffer for the sector
 32596                                  ;		    the buffer type bits OF buf_flags = 0, caller must set it
 32597                                  ;	USES	AX, BX, CX, SI, DI, Flags
 32598                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 33353                                  ;**	Process related system calls and low level routines for DOS 2.X.

 33365                                  ;
 33366                                  ;		Created: ARR 30 March 1983
 33367                                  ;		AN000	version 4.0 jan. 1988

 33375                                  ;		M005 - Support for EXE programs with out STACK segment and 
 33376                                  ;		       with resident size < 64K - 256 bytes. A 256 byte 
 33377                                  ;		       stack is provided at the end of the program. Note that
 33378                                  ;		       only SP is changed.

 33380                                  ;

 33384                                  ;			in memory block >= 64K, sp = 0. If memory block
 33385                                  ;			obtained is <64K, point sp at the end of the memory
 33386                                  ;			block. For EXEs smaller than 64K, 256 bytes are still
 33387                                  ;			added for a stack segment which may be needed if it

 33391                                  ;

 33393                                  ;			a bad environment if it reached 32767 bytes. Changed

 33455                                  ; =========================================================================
 33456                                  ;BREAK <$exec - load/go a program>
 33457                                  ;	EXEC.ASM - EXEC System Call
 33458                                  ;
 33459                                  ;
 33460                                  ; Assembler usage:
 33461                                  ;	    lds     DX, Name
 33462                                  ;	    les     BX, Blk
 33463                                  ;	    mov     AH, Exec
 33464                                  ;	    mov     AL, FUNC
 33465                                  ;	    int     INT_COMMAND
 33466                                  ;
 33467                                  ;	AL  Function
 33468                                  ;	--  --------
 33469                                  ;	 0  Load and execute the program.
 33470                                  ;	 1  Load, create the program header but do not
 33471                                  ;	    begin execution.
 33472                                  ;	 3  Load overlay. No header created.
 33473                                  ;
 33474                                  ;	    AL = 0 -> load/execute program
 33475                                  ;
 33476                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33477                                  ;	    | WORD segment address of	|
 33478                                  ;	    | environment.		|
 33479                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33480                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to ASCIZ	|
 33481                                  ;	    | command line at 80h	|
 33482                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33483                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33484                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 5Ch	|
 33485                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33486                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33487                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 6Ch	|
 33488                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33489                                  ;
 33490                                  ;	    AL = 1 -> load program
 33491                                  ;
 33492                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33493                                  ;	    | WORD segment address of	|
 33494                                  ;	    | environment.		|
 33495                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33496                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to ASCIZ	|
 33497                                  ;	    | command line at 80h	|
 33498                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33499                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33500                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 5Ch	|
 33501                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33502                                  ;	    | DWORD pointer to default	|
 33503                                  ;	    | FCB to be passed at 6Ch	|
 33504                                  ;	    +---------------------------+
 33505                                  ;	    | DWORD returned value of	|

 33614                                  	; possibility that the count may not be decremented all the way to

 33616                                  	; the A20 off for a sufficiently long time (A20OFF_COUNT int 21 
 33617                                  	; calls), exits pre-maturely due to error conditions.
 33618

 35521                                  ;**	Coalesce - Combine free blocks ahead with current block
 35522                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35523                                  ;	Coalesce adds the block following the argument to the argument block,
 35524                                  ;	iff it's free.  Coalesce is usually used to join free blocks, but
 35525                                  ;	some callers (such as $setblock) use it to join a free block to it's
 35526                                  ;	preceeding allocated block.
 35527                                  ;
 35528                                  ;	ENTRY	(ds) = pointer to the head of a free block
 35529                                  ;		(di) = 0
 35530                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 35531                                  ;		  (ds) unchanged, this block updated
 35532                                  ;		  (ax) = address of next block, IFF not at end
 35533                                  ;		'C' set if arena trashed
 35534                                  ;	USES	(cx)
 35535                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35536                                          
 35537                                  Coalesce:
 35538                                  	;cmp	byte [di],5Ah ; 'Z'
 35539 000060CD 803D5A                  	CMP     BYTE [DI],arena_signature_end
 35540                                                                          ; IF current signature = END THEN
 35541                                          ;retz				;   GOTO ok

 35544                                          ;retc				; IF no error THEN GOTO check

 35562                                  ; IBMDOS.COM (MSDOS 3.3, 1987) - Offset 641Fh

 35564                                  ;	BREAK  <$Alloc - allocate space in memory>
 35565                                  
 35566                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 35567                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35568                                  ;**	$Alloc - Allocate Memory Space
 35569                                  ;
 35570                                  ;	$Alloc services the INT21 that allocates memory space to a program.
 35571                                  ;	Alloc returns a pointer to a free block of memory that
 35572                                  ;	has the requested size in paragraphs.
 35573                                  ;
 35574                                  ;	If the allocation strategy is HIGH_FIRST or HIGH_ONLY memory is 
 35575                                  ;	scanned from umb_head if not from arena_head. If the strategy is
 35576                                  ; 	HIGH_FIRST the scan is continued from arena_head if a block of 
 35577                                  ;	appropriate size is not found in the UMBs. If the strategy is 
 35578                                  ;	HIGH_FIRST+HIGH_ONLY only the UMBs are scanned for memory.
 35579                                  ;
 35580                                  ;	In either case if bit 0 of UmbFlag is not initialized then the scan
 35581                                  ;	starts from arena_head.
 35582                                  ;
 35583                                  ;	Assembler usage:
 35584                                  ;           MOV     BX,size
 35585                                  ;           MOV     AH,Alloc
 35586                                  ;           INT     21h
 35587                                  ;
 35588                                  ;	BUGBUG - a lot can be done to improve performance. We can set marks
 35589                                  ;	so that we start searching the arena at it's first non-trivial free
 35590                                  ;	block, we can peephole the code, etc. (We can move some subr calls
 35591                                  ;	inline, etc.) I assume that this is called rarely and that the arena
 35592                                  ;	doesn't have too many memory objects in it beyond the first free one.
 35593                                  ;	verify that this is true; if so, this can stay as is
 35594                                  ;
 35595                                  ;	ENTRY	(bx) = requested size, in bytes
 35596                                  ;		(DS) = (ES) = DOSGROUP
 35597                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if memory allocated
 35598                                  ;		  (ax:0) = address of requested memory
 35599                                  ;		'C' set if request failed
 35600                                  ;		  (AX) = error_not_enough_memory
 35601                                  ;		    (bx) = max size we could have allocated
 35602                                  ;		  (ax) = error_arena_trashed
 35603                                  ;	USES	All
 35604                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35605                                  
 35606                                  ; MSDOS 2.11 (& MSDOS 3.3)
 35607                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35608                                  ;SUBTTL $Alloc - allocate space in memory
 35609                                  ;
 35610                                  ;   Assembler usage:
 35611                                  ;           MOV     BX,size
 35612                                  ;           MOV     AH,Alloc
 35613                                  ;           INT     21h
 35614                                  ;         AX:0 is pointer to allocated memory
 35615                                  ;         BX is max size if not enough memory
 35616                                  ;
 35617                                  ;   Description:
 35618                                  ;           Alloc returns  a  pointer  to  a  free  block of
 35619                                  ;       memory that has the requested  size  in  paragraphs.
 35620                                  ;
 35621                                  ;   Error return:
 35622                                  ;           AX = error_not_enough_memory
 35623                                  ;              = error_arena_trashed
 35624                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35625

 35960                                  ;	BREAK $SETBLOCK - change size of an allocated block (if possible)
 35961                                  
 35962                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 35963                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35964                                  ;**	$SETBLOCK - Change size of an Allocated Block
 35965                                  ;
 35966                                  ;	Setblock changes the size of an allocated block. First, we coalesce
 35967                                  ;	any following free space onto this block; then we try to trim the
 35968                                  ;	block down to the size requested.
 35969                                  ;
 35970                                  ;	Note that if the guy wants to grow the block but that growth fails,
 35971                                  ;	we still go ahead and coalesce any trailing free blocks onto it.
 35972                                  ;	Thus the maximum-size-possible value that we return has already
 35973                                  ;	been allocated! This is a bug, dare we fix it? BUGBUG
 35974                                  ;
 35975                                  ;	NOTE - $SETBLOCK is in bed with $ALLOC and jumps into $ALLOC to
 35976                                  ;		finish it's work. For this reason we build the allocsf
 35977                                  ;		structure on the frame, to make us compatible with $ALLOCs
 35978                                  ;		code.
 35979                                  ;
 35980                                  ;	ENTRY	(es) = segment of old block
 35981                                  ;		(bx) = newsize
 35982                                  ;		(ah) = SETBLOCK
 35983                                  ;
 35984                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 35985                                  ;		'C' set if error
 35986                                  ;		  (ax) = error_invalid_block
 35987                                  ;		       = error_arena_trashed
 35988                                  ;		       = error_not_enough_memory
 35989                                  ;		       = error_invalid_function
 35990                                  ;		  (bx) = maximum size possible, iff (ax) = error_not_enough_memory
 35991                                  ;	USES	???? BUGBUG
 35992                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35993                                  
 35994                                  ; MSDOS 2.11 (& MSDOS 3.3)
 35995                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35996                                  ;SUBTTL $SETBLOCK - change size of an allocated block (if possible)
 35997                                  ;
 35998                                  ;   Assembler usage:
 35999                                  ;           MOV     ES,block
 36000                                  ;           MOV     BX,newsize
 36001                                  ;           MOV     AH,setblock
 36002                                  ;           INT     21h
 36003                                  ;         if setblock fails for growing, BX will have the maximum
 36004                                  ;         size possible
 36005                                  ;   Error return:
 36006                                  ;           AX = error_invalid_block
 36007                                  ;              = error_arena_trashed
 36008                                  ;              = error_not_enough_memory
 36009                                  ;              = error_invalid_function
 36010                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36011                                  
 36012                                  _$SETBLOCK:        
 36013                                  	; 04/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 36014                                  	;EnterCrit   critMem
 36015 00006240 E8A4B0                  	call	ECritMEM ; MSDOS 3.3 & MSDOS 6.0

 36106                                  ;	BREAK $AllocOper - get/set allocation mechanism
 36107                                  
 36108                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 36109                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36110                                  ;**	$AllocOper - Get/Set Allocation Mechanism
 36111                                  ;
 36112                                  ;	Assembler usage:
 36113                                  ;           MOV     AH,AllocOper
 36114                                  ;           MOV     BX,method
 36115                                  ;           MOV     AL,func
 36116                                  ;           INT     21h
 36117                                  ;
 36118                                  ;	ENTRY	
 36119                                  ;		(al) = 0
 36120                                  ;		  Get allocation Strategy in (ax)
 36121                                  ;
 36122                                  ;		(al) = 1, (bx) = method = zw0000xy
 36123                                  ;		  Set allocation strategy.
 36124                                  ;		   w  = 1  => HIGH_ONLY
 36125                                  ;		   z  = 1  => HIGH_FIRST
 36126                                  ;		   xy = 00 => FIRST_FIT
 36127                                  ;		      = 01 => BEST_FIT
 36128                                  ;		      = 10 => LAST_FIT
 36129                                  ;
 36130                                  ;		(al) = 2
 36131                                  ;		  Get UMB link state in (al)
 36132                                  ;
 36133                                  ;		(al) = 3
 36134                                  ;		  Set UMB link state
 36135                                  ;		   (bx) = 0 => Unlink UMBs
 36136                                  ;		   (bx) = 1 => Link UMBs
 36137                                  ;
 36138                                  ;
 36139                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 36140                                  ;
 36141                                  ;		 if (al) = 0
 36142                                  ;		  (ax) = existing method
 36143                                  ;		 if (al) = 1
 36144                                  ;		  Sets allocation strategy
 36145                                  ;		 if (al) = 2
 36146                                  ;		  (al) = 0 => UMBs not linked
 36147                                  ;		  (al) = 1 => UMBs linked in
 36148                                  ;		 if (al) = 3
 36149                                  ;		  Links/Unlinks the UMBs into DOS chain
 36150                                  ;
 36151                                  ;		'C' set if error
 36152                                  ;		  AX = error_invalid_function
 36153                                  ;
 36154                                  ;	Rev. M000 - added support for HIGH_FIRST in (al) = 1. 7/9/90
 36155                                  ; 	Rev. M003 - added functions (al) = 2 and (al) = 3. 7/18/90
 36156                                  ;	Rev. M009 - (al) = 3 will return 'invalid function' in ax if
 36157                                  ;		    umbhead has'nt been initialized by sysinit and 'trashed
 36158                                  ;		    arena' if an arena sig is damaged.
 36159                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36160                                  
 36161                                  ; MSDOS 2.11 (& MSDOS 3.3)
 36162                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 36873                                  ;	BREAK	<pJFNFromHandle - return pointer to JFN table entry>
 36874                                  
 36875                                  ;**	pJFNFromHandle - Translate Handle to Pointer to JFN
 36876                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36877                                  ;	pJFNFromHandle takes a file handle and turns that into a pointer to
 36878                                  ;	the JFN entry (i.e., to a byte holding the internal file handle #)
 36879                                  ;
 36880                                  ;	NOTE:
 36881                                  ;	  This routine is called from $CREATE_PROCESS_DATA_BLOCK which is called
 36882                                  ;	  at DOSINIT time with SS NOT DOSGROUP
 36883                                  ;
 36884                                  ;	ENTRY	(bx) = handle
 36885                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if ok
 36886                                  ;		  (es:di) = address of JFN value
 36887                                  ;		'C' set if error
 36888                                  ;		  (ax) = error code
 36889                                  ;	USES	AX, DI, ES, Flags
 36890                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36891                                  
 36892                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 36893                                  
 36894                                  pJFNFromHandle:
 36895                                  	; 05/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 36896                                  	;getdseg <es>			; es -> dosdata
 36897 000064A3 2E8E06[0700]            	mov	es,[cs:DosDSeg]
 36898                                  	
 36899                                  	;MOV	ES,[cs:CurrentPDB]	; get user process data block
 36900 000064A8 268E06[3003]            	mov	es,[es:CurrentPDB]
 36901                                  
 36902                                  	;cmp	bx,[ES:32h]
 36903 000064AD 263B1E3200              	CMP	BX,[ES:PDB.JFN_Length]	; is handle greater than allocated
 36904 000064B2 7204                    	JB	short pjfn10		; no, get offset
 36905                                  ReturnCarry_inv_hndl: ; 05/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 36906                                  	;mov	al,6
 36907 000064B4 B006                    	MOV     AL,error_invalid_handle ; appropriate error
 36908                                  ReturnCarry:
 36909 000064B6 F9                      	STC                             ; signal error
 36910 000064B7 C3                      	retn				; go back
 36911                                  pjfn10: 
 36912                                  	;les	di,[es:34h]
 36913 000064B8 26C43E3400              	LES	DI,[ES:PDB.JFN_Pointer]	; get pointer to beginning of table
 36914 000064BD 01DF                    	ADD	DI,BX			; add in offset, clear 'C'
 36915                                  	;clc
 36916                                  pJFNFromHandle_error:
 36917 000064BF C3                      	retn

 36919                                  ;BREAK <SFFromHandle - return pointer (or error) to SF entry from handle>
 36920                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36921                                  ;
 36922                                  ; Procedure Name : SFFromHandle
 36923                                  ;
 36924                                  ; SFFromHandle - Given a handle, get JFN and then index into SF table
 36925                                  ;
 36926                                  ;   Input:      BX has handle
 36927                                  ;   Output:     Carry Set
 36928                                  ;                   AX has error code
 36929                                  ;               Carry Reset
 36930                                  ;                   ES:DI has pointer to SF entry
 36931                                  ;   Registers modified: If error, AX,ES, else ES:DI
 36932                                  ; NOTE:
 36933                                  ;   This routine is called from $CREATE_PROCESS_DATA_BLOCK which is called
 36934                                  ;       at DOSINIT time with SS NOT DOSGROUP
 36935                                  ;
 36936                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36937                                  
 36938                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 36939                                  
 36940                                  SFFromHandle:
 36941 000064C0 E8E0FF                  	CALL	pJFNFromHandle		; get jfn pointer
 36942                                  	;retc				; return if error
 36943 000064C3 72FA                    	jc	short pJFNFromHandle_error
 36944 000064C5 26803DFF                	CMP     BYTE [ES:DI],-1		; unused handle
 36945                                  	;JNZ	short GetSF		; nope, suck out SF
 36946                                  	;;mov	al,6
 36947                                  	;MOV	AL,error_invalid_handle ; appropriate error
 36948                                  	;jmp	short ReturnCarry	; signal it
 36949                                  	; 17/12/2022
 36950                                  	; 02/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 36951 000064C9 74E9                    	jz	short ReturnCarry_inv_hndl ; Retro DOS v3.0 modification
 36952                                  	;JNZ	short GetSF		; nope, suck out SF
 36953                                  	;;mov	al,6
 36954                                  	;MOV	AL,error_invalid_handle ; appropriate error
 36955                                  	;jmp	short ReturnCarry	; signal it
 36956                                  GetSF:
 36957 000064CB 53                      	push	bx			; save handle
 36958 000064CC 268A1D                  	MOV     BL,[ES:DI]		; get SFN
 36959 000064CF 30FF                    	XOR     BH,BH                   ; ignore upper half
 36960 000064D1 E80200                  	CALL    SFFromSFN               ; get real sf spot
 36961 000064D4 5B                      	pop	bx			; restore
 36962 000064D5 C3                      	retn                        	; say goodbye
 36963                                  
 36964                                  ;BREAK <SFFromSFN - index into SF table for SFN>
 36965                                  
 36966                                  ;**	SFFromSFN - Get an SF Table entry from an SFN
 36967                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36968                                  ;	SFFromSfn uses an SFN to index an entry into the SF table. This
 36969                                  ;	is more than just a simple index instruction because the SF table
 36970                                  ;	can be made up of multiple pieces chained together. We follow the
 36971                                  ;	chain to the right piece and then do the index operation.
 36972                                  ;
 36973                                  ;   NOTE:
 36974                                  ;	This routine is called from SFFromHandle which is called
 36975                                  ;       at DOSINIT time with SS NOT DOSGROUP
 36976                                  ;
 36977                                  ;	ENTRY	BX has SF index
 36978                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 36979                                  ;		  ES:DI points to SF entry
 36980                                  ;		'C' set if index too large
 36981                                  ;	USES	BX, DI, ES
 36982                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36983                                  
 36984                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 36985                                  
 36986                                  SFFromSFN:
 36987                                  	; 05/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 36988                                  	;getdseg <es>			; es -> dosdata
 36989 000064D6 2E8E06[0700]            	mov	es,[cs:DosDSeg]
 36990                                  
 36991                                  	;LES	DI,[CS:SFT_ADDR]	; (es:di) = start of SFT table
 36992 000064DB 26C43E[2A00]            	les	di,[es:SFT_ADDR]
 36993                                  sfsfn5:	
 36994                                  	;cmp	bx,[es:di+4]
 36995 000064E0 263B5D04                	CMP	BX,[ES:DI+SFT.SFCount]	; is handle in this table?
 36996 000064E4 720E                    	JB	short sfsfn7		; yes, go grab it
 36997                                  	;sub	bx,[es:di+4]
 36998 000064E6 262B5D04                	SUB     BX,[ES:DI+SFT.SFCount]
 36999 000064EA 26C43D                  	les	di,[es:di] ; 14/08/2018
 37000                                  	;LES	DI,[ES:DI+SFT.SFLink]	; get next table segment
 37001 000064ED 83FFFF                  	CMP     DI,-1                   ; end of tables?
 37002 000064F0 75EE                    	JNZ	short sfsfn5		; no, try again
 37003 000064F2 F9                      	STC
 37004 000064F3 C3                      	retn				; return with error, not found
 37005                                  sfsfn7:
 37006 000064F4 50                      	push	ax
 37007                                  	;mov	ax,53 ; MSDOS 3.3
 37008                                  	;mov	ax,59 ; MSDOS 6.0
 37009                                  	;MOV	AX,SF_ENTRY.size	; put it in a nice place
 37010                                  	
 37011                                  	; 17/12/2022
 37012 000064F5 B03B                    	mov	al,SF_ENTRY.size ; 28/05/2019
 37013                                  	; 07/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 37014                                  	;mov	ax,SF_ENTRY.size ; 59
 37015                                  	
 37016 000064F7 F6E3                    	MUL	BL			; (ax) = offset into this SF block
 37017 000064F9 01C7                    	ADD	DI,AX			; add base of SF block
 37018 000064FB 58                      	pop	ax
 37019                                  	;add	di,6
 37020 000064FC 83C706                  	ADD	DI,SFT.SFTable		; offset into structure, 'C' cleared
 37021 000064FF C3                      	retn				; return with 'C' clear
 37022                                  
 37023                                  ;	BREAK <JFNFree - return a jfn pointer if one is free>
 37024                                  
 37025                                  ;**	JFNFree - Find a Free JFN Slot
 37026                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37027                                  ;	JFNFree scansthrough the JFN table and returnsa pointer to a free slot
 37028                                  ;
 37029                                  ;	ENTRY	(ss) = DOSDATA
 37030                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 37031                                  ;		  (bx) = new handle
 37032                                  ;		  (es:di) = pointer to JFN slot
 37033                                  ;		'C' set if error
 37034                                  ;		  (al) = error code
 37035                                  ;	USES	bx, di, es, flags
 37036                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37037                                  
 37038                                  JFNFree:
 37039 00006500 31DB                    	XOR	BX,BX			; (bx) = initial JFN to try
 37040                                  jfnf1:	
 37041 00006502 E89EFF                  	CALL	pJFNFromHandle		; get the appropriate handle
 37042 00006505 7209                    	JC	short jfnf5		; no more handles
 37043 00006507 26803DFF                	CMP     BYTE [ES:DI],-1		; free?
 37044 0000650B 7405                    	je	short jfnfx		; yes, carry is clear
 37045 0000650D 43                      	INC     BX                      ; no, next handle
 37046 0000650E EBF2                    	JMP	short jfnf1		; and try again
 37047                                  
 37048                                  	; Error. 'C' set
 37049                                  jfnf5:	
 37050                                  	;mov	al,4
 37051 00006510 B004                    	MOV	AL,error_too_many_open_files
 37052                                  jfnfx:	
 37053 00006512 C3                      	retn				; bye
 37054                                  
 37055                                  ;	BREAK <SFNFree - Allocate a free SFN>
 37056                                  
 37057                                  ;**	SFNFree - Allocate a Free SFN/SFT
 37058                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37059                                  ;	SFNFree scans through the sf table looking for a free entry
 37060                                  ;	If it finds one it partially allocates it by setting SFT_REF_COUNT = -1
 37061                                  ;
 37062                                  ;	The problem is that we want to mark the SFT busy so that other threads
 37063                                  ;	can't allocate the SFT before we're finished marking it up.  However,
 37064                                  ;	we can't just mark it busy because we may get blown out of our open
 37065                                  ;	by INT24 and leave the thing orphaned.	To solve this we mark it
 37066                                  ;	"allocation in progress" by setting SFT_REF_COUNT = -1.  If we see
 37067                                  ;	an SFT with this value we look to see if it belongs to this user
 37068                                  ;	and process.  If it does belong to us then it must be an orphan
 37069                                  ;	and we reclaim it.
 37070                                  ;
 37071                                  ;	BUGBUG - improve the performance. I guess it's smaller to call SFFromSFN
 37072                                  ;		over and over, but we could at least set a high water mark...
 37073                                  ;		cause an N^2 loop calling slow SFFromSFN is real slow, too slow
 37074                                  ;		even though this is not a frequently called routine - jgl
 37075                                  ;
 37076                                  ;	ENTRY	(ss) = DOSDATA
 37077                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if no error
 37078                                  ;		  (bx) = SFN
 37079                                  ;		  (es:di) = pointer to SFT
 37080                                  ;		  es:[di].SFT_REF_COUNT = -1
 37081                                  ;		'C' set if error
 37082                                  ;		  (al) = error code
 37083                                  ;	USES	bx, di, es, Flags
 37084                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37085                                  
 37086                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37087                                  	; DOSCODE:A682h (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37088                                  
 37089                                  SFNFree:
 37090                                  	; 12/08/2018
 37091                                  	; 05/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 37092                                  	;
 37093                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 37094 00006513 50                      	push	ax
 37095 00006514 31DB                    	xor	bx,bx			; (bx) = SFN to consider
 37096                                  sfnf5:	
 37097 00006516 53                      	push	bx
 37098 00006517 E8BCFF                  	call	SFFromSFN		; get the potential handle
 37099 0000651A 5B                      	pop	bx
 37100 0000651B 723A                    	jc	short sfnf95		; no more free SFNs
 37101 0000651D 26833D00                	cmp	word [ES:DI],0
 37102                                  	;cmp	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_Ref_Count],0 ; free?
 37103 00006521 741D                    	je	short sfnf20			; yep, got one
 37104                                  	
 37105                                  	;cmp	word [es:di],0FFFFh ; -1
 37106 00006523 26833DFF                	cmp	word [ES:DI],sf_busy
 37107                                  	;cmp	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count],sf_busy
 37108 00006527 7403                    	je	short sfnf10		; special busy mark
 37109                                  sfnf7:	
 37110 00006529 43                      	inc	bx			; try the next one
 37111 0000652A EBEA                    	jmp	short sfnf5
 37112                                  
 37113                                  ;	The SFT has the special "busy" mark; if it belongs to us then
 37114                                  ;	it was abandoned during a earlier call and we can use it.
 37115                                  ;
 37116                                  ;	(bx)	= SFN
 37117                                  ;	(es:di) = pointer to SFT
 37118                                  ;	(TOS)	= caller's (ax)
 37119                                  
 37120                                  sfnf10:	
 37121 0000652C 36A1[3E03]              	mov	ax,[SS:USER_ID]
 37122                                  	;cmp	[es:di+2Fh],ax
 37123 00006530 2639452F                	cmp	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_UID],ax
 37124 00006534 75F3                    	jnz	short sfnf7		; not ours
 37125 00006536 36A1[3C03]              	mov	ax,[SS:PROC_ID]
 37126                                  	;cmp	[es:di+31h],ax
 37127 0000653A 26394531                	cmp	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_PID],ax
 37128 0000653E 75E9                    	jnz	short sfnf7		; can't use this one, try the next
 37129                                  
 37130                                  ;	We have an SFT to allocate
 37131                                  ;
 37132                                  ;	(bx)	= SFN
 37133                                  ;	(es:di) = pointer to SFT
 37134                                  ;	(TOS)	= caller's (ax)
 37135                                  
 37136                                  sfnf20:
 37137                                  	; cf = 0 ;; Retro DOS v3.0
 37138                                  
 37139                                  	;mov	word [es:di],0FFFFh
 37140 00006540 26C705FFFF              	mov	word [ES:DI],sf_busy
 37141                                  					; make sure that this is allocated
 37142                                  	;mov	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count],sf_busy
 37143                                  
 37144 00006545 36A1[3E03]              	mov	ax,[SS:USER_ID]
 37145                                  	;mov	[es:di+2Fh],ax
 37146 00006549 2689452F                	mov	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_UID],ax
 37147 0000654D 36A1[3C03]              	mov	ax,[SS:PROC_ID]
 37148                                  	;mov	[es:di+31h],ax
 37149 00006551 26894531                	mov	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_PID],ax
 37150                                  sfnf21: ;; Retro DOS v3.0
 37151                                  	; 02/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 37152                                  	;pop	ax
 37153                                  	;;clc
 37154                                  	;retn				; return with no error
 37155                                  	; 17/12/2022
 37156 00006555 58                      	pop	ax
 37157                                  	;clc
 37158 00006556 C3                      	retn
 37159                                  
 37160                                  ;**	Error - no more free SFNs
 37161                                  ;
 37162                                  ;	'C' set
 37163                                  ;	(TOS) = saved ax
 37164                                  
 37165                                  sfnf95: 
 37166 00006557 58                      	pop	ax
 37167                                  
 37168                                  ; 11/03/2024
 37169                                  %if 0
 37170                                  	;mov	al,4
 37171                                  	mov	al,error_too_many_open_files
 37172                                  	retn				; return with 'C' and error
 37173                                  %else
 37174                                  	; 11/03/2024
 37175 00006558 EBB6                    	jmp	short jfnf5
 37176                                  %endif

 37186                                  ;	BREAK <$Close - return a handle to the system>
 37187                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37188                                  ;
 37189                                  ;**	$Close - Close a file Handle
 37190                                  ;
 37191                                  ;	BUGBUG - close gets called a LOT with invalid handles - sizzle that
 37192                                  ;		path
 37193                                  ;
 37194                                  ;	Assembler usage:
 37195                                  ;	    MOV     BX, handle
 37196                                  ;	    MOV     AH, Close
 37197                                  ;	    INT     int_command
 37198                                  ;
 37199                                  ;	ENTRY	(bx) = handle
 37200                                  ;	EXIT	<normal INT21 return convention>
 37201                                  ;	USES	all
 37202                                  ;
 37203                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37204                                  
 37205                                  ; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37206                                  ; DOSCODE:A6CBh (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 37207                                  
 37208                                  _$CLOSE:
 37209                                  ;	Grab the SFT pointer from the JFN.
 37210                                  
 37211 0000655A E84802                  	call	CheckOwner		; get system file entry
 37212 0000655D 722B                    	jc	short CloseError	; error return
 37213 0000655F 16                      	push	ss
 37214 00006560 1F                      	pop	ds			; For DOS_CLOSE
 37215 00006561 893E[9E05]              	MOV	[THISSFT],DI		; save offset of pointer
 37216 00006565 8C06[A005]              	MOV	[THISSFT+2],ES		; save segment value
 37217                                  
 37218                                  ; DS:SI point to JFN table entry.
 37219                                  ; ES:DI point to SFT
 37220                                  ;
 37221                                  ; We now examine the user's JFN entry; If the file was a 70-mode file (network
 37222                                  ; FCB, we examine the ref count on the SFT; if it was 1, we free the JFN.
 37223                                  ; If the file was not a net FCB, we free the JFN too.
 37224                                  
 37225                                  	;CMP	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count],1
 37226 00006569 26833D01                	cmp	word [ES:DI],1		; will the SFT become free?
 37227 0000656D 740A                    	jz	short FreeJFN 		; yes, free JFN anyway.
 37228                                  	;mov	al,[ES:DI+2]
 37229 0000656F 268A4502                	MOV	AL,[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_mode]
 37230                                  	;and	al,0F0h
 37231 00006573 24F0                    	AND	AL,SHARING_MASK
 37232                                  	;cmp	al,70h
 37233 00006575 3C70                    	CMP	AL,SHARING_NET_FCB
 37234 00006577 7407                    	JZ	short PostFree		; 70-mode and big ref count => free it
 37235                                  
 37236                                  ; The JFN must be freed. Get the pointer to it and replace the contents with
 37237                                  ; -1.
 37238                                  
 37239                                  FreeJFN:
 37240 00006579 E827FF                  	call	pJFNFromHandle		; d = pJFN (handle);
 37241 0000657C 26C605FF                	MOV	BYTE [ES:DI],0FFh	; release the JFN
 37242                                  PostFree:
 37243                                  
 37244                                  ; ThisSFT is correctly set, we have DS = DOSDATA. Looks OK for a DOS_CLOSE!
 37245                                  
 37246 00006580 E8E6C8                  	call	DOS_CLOSE
 37247                                  
 37248                                  ; DOS_Close may return an error. If we see such an error, we report it but
 37249                                  ; the JFN stays closed because DOS_Close always frees the SFT!
 37250                                  
 37251 00006583 7205                    	JC	short CloseError
 37252                                  	;mov	ah,3Eh
 37253 00006585 B43E                    	MOV	AH,CLOSE		; MZ Bogus multiplan fix
 37254                                  	; 02/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 37255                                  CloseOk:
 37256 00006587 E9ABA0                  	jmp	SYS_RET_OK
 37257                                  CloseError:
 37258                                  CommitError:	; 11/03/2024
 37259 0000658A E9B1A0                  	jmp	SYS_RET_ERR
 37260                                  
 37261                                  ;	BREAK <$Commit - commit the file>
 37262                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37263                                  ;
 37264                                  ;**	$Commit - Commit a File
 37265                                  ;
 37266                                  ;	$Commit "commits" a file to disk - all of it's buffers are
 37267                                  ;	flushed out. BUGBUG - I'm pretty sure that $Commit doesn't update

 37315                                  ;	BREAK <$ExtHandle - extend handle count>
 37316                                  
 37317                                  ;**	$ExtHandle - Extend Handle Count
 37318                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37319                                  ;	Assembler usage:

 38062                                  ;Break	<CheckOwner - verify ownership of handles from server>

 38064                                  ;   CheckOwner - Due to the ability of the server to close file handles for a
 38065                                  ;   process without the process knowing it (delete/rename of open files, for
 38066                                  ;   example), it is possible for the redirector to issue a call to a handle
 38067                                  ;   that it soes not rightfully own. We check here to make sure that the
 38068                                  ;   issuing process is the owner of the SFT. At the same time, we do a
 38069                                  ;   SFFromHandle to really make sure that the SFT is good.

 38126                                  ;	TITLE	MACRO - Pathname and macro related internal routines
 38127                                  ;	NAME	MACRO
 38128                                  
 38129                                  ;	Microsoft Confidential
 38130                                  ;	Copyright (C) Microsoft Corporation 1991
 38131                                  ;	All Rights Reserved.
 38132                                  
 38133                                  ;**	MACRO.ASM
 38134                                  ;
 38135                                  ;	$AssignOper
 38136                                  ;	FIND_DPB
 38137                                  ;	InitCDS
 38138                                  ;	$UserOper
 38139                                  ;	GetVisDrv
 38140                                  ;	GetThisDrv
 38141                                  ;	GetCDSFromDrv
 38142                                  ;
 38143                                  ;   Revision history:
 38144                                  ;
 38145                                  ;	Created: MZ 4 April 1983
 38146                                  ;		 MZ 18 April 1983   Make TransFCB handle extended FCBs
 38147                                  ;		 AR 2 June 1983     Define/Delete macro for NET redir.
 38148                                  ;		 MZ 3 Nov 83	    Fix InitCDS to reset length to 2
 38149                                  ;		 MZ 4 Nov 83	    Fix NetAssign to use STRLEN only
 38150                                  ;		 MZ 18 Nov 83	    Rewrite string processing for subtree
 38151                                  ;				    aliasing.
 38152                                  ;
 38153                                  ;   MSDOS performs several types of name translation. First, we maintain for
 38154                                  ;   each valid drive letter the text of the current directory on that drive.
 38155                                  ;   For invalid drive letters, there is no current directory so we pretend to
 38156                                  ;   be at the root. A current directory is either the raw local directory
 38157                                  ;   (consisting of drive:\path) or a local network directory (consisting of
 38158                                  ;   \\machine\path. There is a limit on the point to which a .. is allowed.
 38159                                  ;
 38160                                  ;   Given a path, MSDOS will transform this into a real from-the-root path
 38161                                  ;   without . or .. entries. Any component that is > 8.3 is truncated to
 38162                                  ;   this and all * are expanded into ?'s.
 38163                                  ;
 38164                                  ;   The second part of name translation involves subtree aliasing. A list of
 38165                                  ;   subtree pairs is maintained by the external utility SUBST. The results of
 38166                                  ;   the previous 'canonicalization' are then examined to see if any of the
 38167                                  ;   subtree pairs is a prefix of the user path. If so, then this prefix is
 38168                                  ;   replaced with the other subtree in the pair.
 38169                                  ;
 38170                                  ;   A third part involves mapping this "real" path into a "physical" path.  A
 38171                                  ;   list of drive/subtree pairs are maintained by the external utility JOIN.
 38172                                  ;   The output of the previous translation is examined to see if any of the
 38173                                  ;   subtrees in this list are a prefix of the string. If so, then the prefix
 38174                                  ;   is replaced by the appropriate drive letter. In this manner, we can
 38175                                  ;   'mount' one device under another.
 38176                                  ;
 38177                                  ;   The final form of name translation involves the mapping of a user's
 38178                                  ;   logical drive number into the internal physical drive. This is
 38179                                  ;   accomplished by converting the drive number into letter:CON, performing
 38180                                  ;   the above translation and then converting the character back into a drive
 38181                                  ;   number.
 38182                                  ;
 38183                                  ;   There are two main entry points: TransPath and TransFCB. TransPath will
 38184                                  ;   take a path and form the real text of the pathname with all . and ..
 38185                                  ;   removed. TransFCB will translate an FCB into a path and then invoke
 38186                                  ;   TransPath.
 38187                                  ;
 38188                                  ;	A000	version 4.00  Jan. 1988
 38189                                  
 38190                                  ;Installed = TRUE
 38191                                  
 38192                                  ;	I_need	ThisCDS,DWORD		; pointer to CDS used
 38193                                  ;	I_need	CDSAddr,DWORD		; pointer to CDS table
 38194                                  ;	I_need	CDSCount,BYTE		; number of CDS entries
 38195                                  ;	I_need	CurDrv,BYTE		; current macro assignment (old
 38196                                  ;					; current drive)
 38197                                  ;	I_need	NUMIO,BYTE		; Number of physical drives
 38198                                  ;	I_need	fSharing,BYTE		; TRUE => no redirection allowed
 38199                                  ;	I_need	DummyCDS,80h		; buffer for dummy cds
 38200                                  ;	I_need	DIFFNAM,BYTE		; flag for MyName being set
 38201                                  ;	I_need	MYNAME,16		; machine name
 38202                                  ;	I_need	MYNUM,WORD		; machine number
 38203                                  ;	I_need	DPBHEAD,DWORD		; beginning of DPB chain
 38204                                  ;	I_need	EXTERR_LOCUS,BYTE	; Extended Error Locus
 38205                                  ;	I_need	DrvErr,BYTE		; drive error
