 45004                                  ;;***************************************************************************
 45005                                  ;; INT 21,52 - Get Pointer to DOS "INVARS" (Undocumented)
 45006                                  ;;
 45007                                  ;;	AH = 52h
 45008                                  ;;
 45009                                  ;;	on return:
 45010                                  ;;	ES:BX = pointer to DOS "invars", a table of pointers used by DOS.
 45011                                  ;;		Known "invars" fields follow (varies with DOS version):
 45012                                  ;;
 45013                                  ;;	Offset Size		 Description
 45014                                  ;;
 45015                                  ;;	 -12   word   sharing retry count (DOS 3.1-3.3)
 45016                                  ;;	 -10   word   sharing retry delay  (DOS 3.1-3.3)
 45017                                  ;;	  -8   dword  pointer to current disk buffer (DOS 3.x)
 45018                                  ;;	  -4   word   pointer in DOS code segment of unread CON input;
 45019                                  ;;		      0 indicates no unread input (DOS 3.x)
 45020                                  ;;	  -2   word   segment of first Memory Control Block (MCB)
 45021                                  ;;	  00   dword  pointer to first DRIVE PARAMETER TABLE (A:) in chain
 45022                                  ;;	  04   dword  pointer to DOS System File Table (SFT)
 45023                                  ;;	  08   dword  pointer to $CLOCK device driver
 45024                                  ;;	  0C   dword  pointer to CON device driver
 45025                                  ;;	  10   byte   number of logical drives in system
 45026                                  ;;	  11   word   maximum bytes/block of any block device
 45027                                  ;;	  13   dword  pointer to DOS cache buffer header
 45028                                  ;;	  17 18bytes  NUL device header, first 4 bytes of device header
 45029                                  ;;		      point to the next device in device chain
 45030                                  ;;
 45031                                  ;;***************************************************************************

 45244                                  
 45245                                  ;Break <Initialized data and data used at DOS initialization>
 45246                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45247                                  
 45248                                  ; We need to identify the parts of the data area that are relevant to tasks
 45249                                  ; and those that are relevant to the system as a whole.  Under 3.0, the system
 45250                                  ; data will be gathered with the system code.  The process data under 2.x will
 45251                                  ; be available for swapping and under 3.0 it will be allocated per-process.
 45252                                  ;
 45253                                  ; The data that is system data will be identified by [SYSTEM] in the comments
 45254                                  ; describing that data item.
 45255                                  
 45256                                  ;DOSDATA SEGMENT WORD PUBLIC 'DATA'
 45257                                  
 45258                                  ;
 45259                                  ; Table of routines for assignable devices
 45260                                  ;
 45261                                  ; MSDOS allows assignment if the following standard devices:
 45262                                  ;   stdin  (usually CON input)
 45263                                  ;   stdout (usually CON output)
 45264                                  ;   auxin  (usually AUX input)
 45265                                  ;   auxout (usually AUX output)
 45266                                  ;   stdlpt (usually PRN output)
 45267                                  ;
 45268                                  ; SPECIAL NOTE:
 45269                                  ;   Status of a file is a strange idea. We choose to handle it in this manner:
 45270                                  ;   If we're not at end-of-file, then we always say that we have a character.
 45271                                  ;   Otherwise, we return ^Z as the character and set the ZERO flag. In this
 45272                                  ;   manner we can support program written under the old DOS (they use ^Z as EOF
 45273                                  ;   on devices) and programs written under the new DOS (they use the ZERO flag
 45274                                  ;   as EOF).
 45275                                  
 45276                                  ; Default SFTs for boot up
 45277                                  
 45278                                  		;PUBLIC	SFTABL
 45279                                  
 45280                                  SFTABL:	   ; LABEL   DWORD		; [SYSTEM] file table
 45281 000000CC FFFF                    		DW -1			; [SYSTEM] link to next table
 45282 000000CE FFFF                    		DW -1			; [SYSTEM] link seg to next table
 45283 000000D0 0500                    		DW sf_default_number	; [SYSTEM] Number of entries in table
 45284                                  		;times 295 db 0 ; MSDOS 6.0
 45285 000000D2 00<rep 127h>            		times (sf_default_number*sf_entry_size) db 0
 45286                                  
 45287                                  ; the next two variables relate to the position of the logical stdout/stdin
 45288                                  ; cursor. They are only meaningful when stdin/stdout are assigned to the
 45289                                  ; console.
 45290                                  		; DOSDATA:01F9h (MSDOS 6.21)
 45291 000001F9 00                      CARPOS:		db 0			; [SYSTEM] cursor position in stdin
 45292 000001FA 00                      STARTPOS:	db 0			; [SYSTEM] position of cursor at beginning
 45293                                  					;	   of buffered input call
 45294 000001FB 00<rep 80h>             INBUF:		times 128 db 0		; [SYSTEM] general device input buffer
 45295 0000027B 00<rep 83h>             CONBUF:		times 131 db 0		; [SYSTEM] The rest of INBUF and console buffer
 45296                                  		; DOSDATA:02FEh (MSDOS 6.21)
 45297 000002FE 00                      PFLAG:		db 0			; [SYSTEM] printer echoing flag

 45300                                  switch_character:

 45508                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------
 45509                                  ; This data section which was named as uninitialized data
 45510                                  ; (as overlayed by initialization code) but follows 
 45511                                  ; initialized data section from DOSDATA:03B6h address
 45512                                  ; (in otherwords, the method is different than MSDOS 3.3,
 45513                                  ; and there is not overlaying..)
 45514                                  ; **********************************************************
 45515                                  ; Reference: MSDOS 6.21 kernel DOSDATA section (4970 bytes)
 45516                                  ; follows DOSCODE section in the kernel file (MSDOS.SYS) 
 45517                                  ; (it is located at offset 0BF70h, file offset 0BF70h-3DE0h) 
 45518                                  ; but starts from offset 0 (ORG 0) and ends at offset 1370h.
 45519                                  ; TIMEBUF is at offset 03B6h.
 45520                                  ; **********************************************************

 45523                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 45974                                  ; DOSDATA:0CF5h
 45975                                  
 45976                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45977                                  ;
 45978                                  ;CASE MAPPER ROUTINE FOR 80H-FFH character range, DOS 3.3
 45979                                  ;     ENTRY: AL = Character to map
 45980                                  ;     EXIT:  AL = The converted character
 45981                                  ; Alters no registers except AL and flags.
 45982                                  ; The routine should do nothing to chars below 80H.
 45983                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45984                                  ; Example:
 45985                                  
 45986                                  MAP_CASE:
 45987                                  ;Procedure MAP_CASE,FAR
 45988                                  
 45989 00000CF5 3C80                    	CMP	AL,80h
 45990 00000CF7 7301                    	JAE	short Map1	;Map no chars below 80H ever
 45991 00000CF9 CB                      	RETF
 45992                                  Map1:
 45993 00000CFA 2C80                    	SUB	AL,80h		;Turn into index value
 45994 00000CFC 1E                      	PUSH	DS
 45995 00000CFD 53                      	PUSH	BX
 45996 00000CFE BB[AF0A]                	MOV	BX,UCASE_TAB+2
 45997                                  FINISH:
 45998 00000D01 0E                      	PUSH	CS		;Move to DS
 45999 00000D02 1F                      	POP	DS
 46000 00000D03 D7                      	XLAT			;Get upper case character
 46001 00000D04 5B                      	POP	BX
 46002 00000D05 1F                      	POP	DS
 46003                                  L_RET:	
 46004 00000D06 CB                      	RETF
 46005                                  
 46006                                  ;EndProc MAP_CASE

 46584                                  ;------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46585                                  ; Patch for Sidekick
 46586                                  ;
 46587                                  ; A documented method for finding the offset of the Errormode flag in the 
 46588                                  ; dos swappable data area if for the app to scan in the dos segment (data) 
 46589                                  ; for the following sequence of instructions.
 46590                                  ;
 46591                                  ; Ref: Part C, Article 11, pg 356 of MSDOS Encyclopedia
 46592                                  ;
 46593                                  ; The Offset of Errormode flag is 0320h
 46594                                  ;
 46595                                  ;------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46596                                  
 46597 00001044 36F6062003FF            	db	036h, 0F6h, 06h, 020h, 03h, 0FFh ; test ss:[errormode], -1
 46598 0000104A 750C                    	db	075h, 0Ch			 ; jnz  NearLabel
 46599 0000104C 36FF365803              	db	036h, 0FFh, 036h, 058h, 03h	 ; push ss:[NearWord]
 46600 00001051 CD28                    	db	0CDh, 028h			 ; int  28h
 46601                                  
 46602                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46603                                  ; Patch for PortOfEntry - M036
 46604                                  ;
 46605                                  ; PortOfEntry by Sector Technology uses an un documented way of determining
 46606                                  ; the offset of Errormode flag. The following patch is to support them in 
 46607                                  ; DOS 5.0. The corresponding code is actually in msdisp.asm
 46608                                  ;
 46609                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46610                                  
 46611 00001053 803E200300              	db 	080h, 03Eh, 020h, 03h, 00h 	 ; cmp 	[errormode], 0
 46612 00001058 7537                    	db	075h, 037h			 ; jnz	NearLabel
 46613 0000105A BCA00A                  	db 	0BCh, 0A0h, 0Ah		  	 ; mov	sp, dosdata:iostack
 46614                                  
 46615                                  %endif ; 29/12/2022

 46672                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46673                                  ;
 46674                                  ; LOW MEM STUB:
 46675                                  ;
 46676                                  ; The low mem stub contains the entry points into DOS for all interrupts 
 46677                                  ; handled by DOS. This stub is installed if the user specifies that the 
 46678                                  ; DOS load in HIMEM. Each entry point does this.
 46679                                  ;
 46680                                  ; 	1. if jmp to 8 has been patched out
 46681                                  ;	   2. if A20 OFF
 46682                                  ;	      3. Enable A20
 46683                                  ;	   4. else 
 46684                                  ;	      5. just go to dos entry
 46685                                  ;	   6. endif
 46686                                  ;	7. else
 46687                                  ;	   8. just go to dos entry
 46688                                  ;	9. endif

 46850                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46851                                  ;
 46852                                  ; LowIntXX:
 46853                                  ;
 46854                                  ; Interrupts from DOS that pass control to a user program must be done from
 46855                                  ; low memory, as the user program may change the state of the A20 line or
 46856                                  ; they may require that the A20 line be OFF. The following piece of code is
 46857                                  ; far call'd from the following places in DOS:
 46858                                  ;
 46859                                  ;	1. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 23h (ctrlc)
 46860                                  ;	2. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 24h (critical error)
 46861                                  ;	3. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 28h (idle int)
 46862                                  ;
 46863                                  ; The int 23 and int 24 handlers may decide to do a far return instead of an
 46864                                  ; IRET ane leave the flags on the stack. Therefore we save the return address
 46865                                  ; before doing the ints and then do a far junp back into DOS.
 46866                                  ;
 46867                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46868                                  
 46869 000010DB 00000000                DosRetAddr23:	dd	0
 46870 000010DF 00000000                DosRetAddr24:	dd	0
 46871 000010E3 00000000                DosRetAddr28:	dd	0
 46872                                  
 46873                                  	; Execute int 23h from low memory
 46874                                  LowInt23:
 46875                                  					; save the return address that is on
 46876                                  					; the stack
 46877 000010E7 2E8F06[DB10]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr23]
 46878 000010EC 2E8F06[DD10]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr23+2]
 46879                                  
 46880 000010F1 CD23                    	int	23h			; ctrl C
 46881                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 46882                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 46883                                  
 46884 000010F3 E87900                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF 
 46885                                  
 46886 000010F6 2EFF2E[DB10]            	jmp	far [cs:DosRetAddr23]	; jump back to DOS
 46887                                  
 46888                                  
 46889                                  	; Execute int 24h from low memory
 46890                                  LowInt24:
 46891                                  					; save the return address that is on
 46892                                  					; the stack
 46893 000010FB 2E8F06[DF10]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr24]
 46894 00001100 2E8F06[E110]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr24+2]
 46895                                  
 46896 00001105 CD24                    	int	24h			; crit error
 46897                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 46898                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 46899                                  
 46900 00001107 E86500                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 46901                                  
 46902 0000110A 2EFF2E[DF10]            	jmp	far [cs:DosRetAddr24]	; jump back to DOS
 46903                                  
 46904                                  
 46905                                   
 46906                                  	; Execute int 28h from low memory
 46907                                  LowInt28:
 46908 0000110F CD28                    	int	28h			; idle int
 46909                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 46910                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 46911                                  
 46912 00001111 E85B00                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 46913                                  
 46914 00001114 CB                      	retf
 46915                                  
 46916                                  ; DOSDATA:1115h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 46917                                  
 46918                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46919                                  ;
 46920                                  ; int 21 ah=4b (exec) call will jump to the following label before xferring
 46921                                  ; control to the exec'd program. We turn off A20 inorder to allow programs
 46922                                  ; that have been packed by the faulty exepack utility to unpack correctly.
 46923                                  ; This is so because exepac'd programs rely on address wrap.
 46924                                  ;
 46925                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46926                                  
 46927                                  disa20_xfer:
 46928 00001115 E83F00                  	call	XMMDisableA20		; disable A20
 46929                                  
 46930                                  	; Look at msproc.asm at label exec_go for understanding the following:
 46931                                  
 46932                                  	; DS:SI points to entry point
 46933                                  	; AX:DI points to initial stack
 46934                                  	; DX has PDB pointer
 46935                                  	; BX has initial AX value
 46936                                  
 46937 00001118 FA                      	cli
 46938 00001119 2EC606[2103]00          	mov	byte [cs:INDOS],0	; SS Override
 46939                                  
 46940 0000111F 8ED0                    	mov	SS,AX			; set up user's stack
 46941 00001121 89FC                    	mov	SP,DI			; and SP
 46942 00001123 FB                      	sti
 46943                                  
 46944 00001124 1E                      	push	DS			; fake long call to entry
 46945 00001125 56                      	push	SI
 46946 00001126 8EC2                    	mov	ES,DX			; set up proper seg registers
 46947 00001128 8EDA                    	mov	DS,DX
 46948 0000112A 89D8                    	mov	AX,BX			; set up proper AX
 46949 0000112C CB                      	retf
 46950                                  
 46951                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46952                                  ;
 46953                                  ; M003:
 46954                                  ;
 46955                                  ; If an int 21 ah=25 call is made immediately after an exec call, DOS will
 46956                                  ; come here, turn A20 OFF restore user stack and registers before returning
 46957                                  ; to user. This is done in dos\msdisp.asm. This has been done to support
 46958                                  ; programs compiled with MS PASCAL 3.2. See under TAG M003 in DOSSYM.INC for
 46959                                  ; more info.	
 46960                                  ;
 46961                                  ; Also at this point DS is DOSDATA. So we can assume DS DOSDATA. Note that
 46962                                  ; SS is also DOS stack. It is important that we do the XMS call on DOS's 
 46963                                  ; stack to avoid additional stack overhead for the user.
 46964                                  ;
 46965                                  ; -------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46966                                  
 46967                                  disa20_iret:
 46968 0000112D E82700                  	call	XMMDisableA20
 46969 00001130 FE0E[2103]              	dec	byte [INDOS]
 46970 00001134 8E16[8605]              	mov	SS,[USER_SS]		; restore user stack
 46971 00001138 8B26[8405]              	mov	SP,[USER_SP]
 46972 0000113C 89E5                    	mov	BP,SP
 46973                                  	;mov	[BP+user_env.user_AX],AL
 46974 0000113E 884600                  	mov	[bp],al
 46975 00001141 A1[F205]                	mov	AX,[NSP]
 46976 00001144 A3[8405]                	mov	[USER_SP],AX
 46977 00001147 A1[F005]                	mov	AX,[NSS]
 46978 0000114A A3[8605]                	mov	[USER_SS],AX
 46979                                  
 46980 0000114D 58                      	pop	AX			; restore user regs
 46981 0000114E 5B                      	pop	BX
 46982 0000114F 59                      	pop	CX
 46983 00001150 5A                      	pop	DX
 46984 00001151 5E                      	pop	SI
 46985 00001152 5F                      	pop	DI
 46986 00001153 5D                      	pop	BP
 46987 00001154 1F                      	pop	DS
 46988 00001155 07                      	pop	ES
 46989 00001156 CF                      	iret
 46990                                  
 46991                                  ;**************************************************************************
 46992                                  ;***	XMMDisableA20 - switch 20th address line
 46993                                  ;
 46994                                  ;	This routine is used to disable the 20th address line in
 46995                                  ;	the system using XMM calls.
 46996                                  ;
 46997                                  ;	ENTRY	none		;ds = _DATA
 46998                                  ;	EXIT	A20 line disabled
 46999                                  ;	USES	NOTHING
 47000                                  ;
 47001                                  ;**************************************************************************
 47002                                  
 47003                                  XMMDisableA20:
 47004 00001157 53                      	push	bx
 47005 00001158 50                      	push	ax
 47006                                  	;mov	ah,XMM_LOCAL_DISABLE_A20
 47007 00001159 B406                    	mov	ah,6
 47008 0000115B 2EFF1E[6311]            	call	far [cs:XMMcontrol]
 47009 00001160 58                      	pop	ax
 47010 00001161 5B                      	pop	bx
 47011 00001162 C3                      	retn
 47012                                  
 47013                                  ; The entry point in the BIOS XMS driver is defined here.
 47014                                  
 47015                                  XMMcontrol:
 47016 00001163 00000000                	dd	0
 47017                                  
 47018                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47019                                  ;
 47020                                  ;***	EnsureA20ON - Ensures that A20 is ON
 47021                                  ;
 47022                                  ;	This routine is used to query the A20 state in
 47023                                  ;	the system using XMM calls.
 47024                                  ;
 47025                                  ;	ENTRY: none
 47026                                  ;
 47027                                  ;	EXIT : A20 will be ON
 47028                                  ;
 47029                                  ; 	USES : NONE
 47030                                  ;
 47031                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47032                                  
 47033                                  LowMemory:	; label dword		; Set equal to 0000:0080
 47034 00001167 8000                    	dw	00080h
 47035 00001169 0000                    	dw	00000h
 47036                                  
 47037                                  HighMemory:	; label dword
 47038 0000116B 9000                    	dw	00090h			; Set equal to FFFF:0090
 47039 0000116D FFFF                    	dw	0FFFFh
 47040                                  
 47041                                  EnsureA20ON:
 47042 0000116F 9C                      	pushf
 47043 00001170 1E                      	push    ds
 47044 00001171 06                      	push	es
 47045 00001172 51                      	push	cx
 47046 00001173 56                      	push	si
 47047 00001174 57                      	push	di
 47048                                  
 47049 00001175 2EC536[6711]            	lds	si,[cs:LowMemory]	; Compare the 4 words at 0000:0080
 47050 0000117A 2EC43E[6B11]            	les	di,[cs:HighMemory]	; with the 4 at FFFF:0090
 47051 0000117F B90400                  	mov	cx,4
 47052 00001182 FC                      	cld
 47053 00001183 F3A7                    	repe    cmpsw
 47054                                  
 47055 00001185 7407                    	jz	short EA20_OFF
 47056                                  EA20_RET:
 47057 00001187 5F                      	pop	di
 47058 00001188 5E                      	pop	si
 47059 00001189 59                      	pop	cx
 47060 0000118A 07                      	pop	es
 47061 0000118B 1F                      	pop	ds
 47062 0000118C 9D                      	popf
 47063 0000118D C3                      	retn
 47064                                  
 47065                                  EA20_OFF:
 47066                                  	; We are going to do the XMS call on the DOS's AuxStack.
 47067                                  	; NOTE: ints are disabled at this point.
 47068                                  
 47069 0000118E 53                      	push	bx
 47070 0000118F 50                      	push	ax
 47071                                  
 47072 00001190 8CD0                    	mov	ax,ss			; save user's stack pointer
 47073 00001192 2EA3[8610]              	mov	[cs:SS_Save],ax
 47074 00001196 2E8926[8810]            	mov	[cs:SP_Save],sp
 47075 0000119B 8CC8                    	mov	ax,cs
 47076 0000119D 8ED0                    	mov	ss,ax
 47077 0000119F BC[A007]                	mov	sp,AUXSTACK
 47078                                  					; ss:sp -> DOSDATA:AuxStack
 47079                                  	;mov	ah,XMM_LOCAL_ENABLE_A20
 47080 000011A2 B405                    	mov	ah,5
 47081 000011A4 2EFF1E[6311]            	call	far [cs:XMMcontrol]
 47082 000011A9 09C0                    	or	ax,ax
 47083 000011AB 740F                    	jz	short XMMerror		; AX = 0 fatal error
 47084                                  
 47085 000011AD 2EA1[8610]              	mov	ax,[cs:SS_Save]		; restore user stack
 47086 000011B1 8ED0                    	mov	ss,ax
 47087 000011B3 2E8B26[8810]            	mov	sp,[cs:SP_Save]
 47088                                  
 47089 000011B8 58                      	pop	ax
 47090 000011B9 5B                      	pop	bx
 47091                                  
 47092 000011BA EBCB                    	jmp	short EA20_RET
 47093                                  
 47094                                  XMMerror:				; M006 - Start
 47095 000011BC B40F                    	mov	ah,0Fh			; get video mode
 47096 000011BE CD10                    	int	10h
 47097 000011C0 3C07                    	cmp	al,7			; Q: are we an MDA
 47098 000011C2 7406                    	je	short XMMcont		; Y: do not change mode
 47099 000011C4 30E4                    	xor	ah,ah ; 0		; set video mode
 47100 000011C6 B002                    	mov	al,02h			; 80 X 25 text
 47101 000011C8 CD10                    	int	10h
 47102                                  XMMcont:
 47103 000011CA B405                    	mov	ah,05h			; set display page
 47104 000011CC 30C0                    	xor	al,al			; page 0
 47105 000011CE CD10                    	int	10h
 47106                                  	
 47107 000011D0 BE[B812]                	mov	si,XMMERRMSG
 47108 000011D3 0E                      	push	cs
 47109 000011D4 1F                      	pop	ds
 47110 000011D5 FC                      	cld				; clear direction flag
 47111                                  XMMprnt:
 47112 000011D6 AC                      	lodsb
 47113 000011D7 3C24                    	cmp	al,'$'			; indicates end of XMMERRMSG
 47114 000011D9 7409                    	jz	short XMMStall		; function 0Eh	
 47115 000011DB B40E                    	mov	ah,0Eh
 47116 000011DD BB0700                  	mov	bx,7
 47117 000011E0 CD10                    	int	10h
 47118 000011E2 EBF2                    	jmp	short XMMprnt
 47119                                  
 47120                                  XMMStall:
 47121 000011E4 FB                      	sti				; allow the user to warm boot
 47122 000011E5 EBFD                    	jmp	short XMMStall		; M006 - End

 47547                                  ; MPATCH.ASM (MSDOS 6.0, 1993)
 47548                                  ;============================================================================
 47549                                  ; 27/04/2019 - Retro DOS 4.0
 47550                                  
 47551                                  ;mpatch.asm -- holds data patch location for callouts 
 47552                                  ; -- allocate cluster in rom.asm
 47553                                  ;
 47554                                  ; This area is pointed to by OffsetMagicPatch[609h] in fixed DOS data.
 47555                                  ; Currently, this location is used only by magicdrv.sys's patch to
 47556                                  ; cluster allocation, however it can be expanded to be used by other
 47557                                  ; patches. This is important since we have an easy-access pointer to
 47558                                  ; this location in OffsetMagicPatch. Magicdrv.sys is guaranteed to
 47559                                  ; only patch out a far call/retf, so any space after that could be
 47560                                  ; used as a patch by using OffsetMagicPatch+6. See rom.asm on how
 47561                                  ; to call out here.
 47562                                  ;
 47563                                  ; Currently, we allocate only the minimum space required for the 6
 47564                                  ; byte magicdrv patch, so if you change the dos data, you may want
 47565                                  ; to reserve space here if your new data will be position dependent
 47566                                  ; and would prohibit growing of this table.
 47567                                  ;       
 47568                                  ;history	-	created 8-7-92 by scottq
 47569                                  ;		-	added Rational386PatchPtr 2-1-93 by jimmat
 47570                                  ;
 47571                                  ;Exported Functions
 47572                                  ;==================
 47573                                  ;MagicPatch     -       callout patched by magidrv.sys for cluster allocations
 47574                                  
 47575                                  ; DosData Segment
 47576                                  
 47577                                  ; DOSDATA:1362h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 47578                                  
 47579                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47580                                  
 47581                                  ; Rational386PatchPtr points to either a RET instruction (80286 or less) or
 47582                                  ; a routine to fix buggy versions of the Rational DOS Extender (80386 or
 47583                                  ; greater). Added to this file because it needed to be somewhere and is
 47584                                  ; 'patch' related.
 47585                                  
 47586                                  Rational386PatchPtr:
 47587                                  	dw	0	; points to patch routine or RET instr.
 47588                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47589                                  
 47590                                  MagicPatch:
 47591                                  ;MagicPatch proc far
 47592                                          retf            ;default is to just return to allocate
 47593                                          nop             ;however, this code will be patched
 47594                                          nop             ;by magicdrv.sys to
 47595                                          nop             ; call far ?:?     
 47596                                          nop             ; retf or perhaps just jmp far
 47597                                          nop             ;retf/nop take one byte, so we need six instructions
 47598                                                          ;for 6 byte patch
 47599                                  ;MagicPatch endp
 47600                                  
 47601                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
